dictionary.title: Word of the Day

senses.definition: Lasting for a very short time; transitory.
senses.example: The ephemeral beauty of cherry blossoms makes them all the more precious.

senses.definition: Something with a very short lifespan, such as an insect that lives only one day.

dictionary.etymology: From Greek ephēmeros: epi- ("on") + hēmera ("day"). Originally referred to a fever lasting only one day.
dictionary.footer: From Greek: epi- (on) + hēmera (day), lasting just one day.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Guide
tips: Say 'WOOS-ter-sheer', drop the 'cester' and 'shire' is just 'sheer'.
The 'ester' in Worcester is silent, it's spelled one way, said another.
Common mistake: 'War-chest-er-shy-er', ignore the spelling entirely.
pronunciation.footer: One of English's most notorious spelling traps.

gloss.title: Astronomy Glossary

entries.definition: The increase in wavelength of electromagnetic radiation as a source moves away from the observer. Higher redshift = more distant / earlier universe.
A position in space where a small object can orbit in a stable pattern relative to two larger ones. JWST sits at L2.
Light with wavelengths longer than visible light (700 nm–1 mm). JWST sees in near-to-mid infrared, which penetrates cosmic dust.
An early, incompletely formed galaxy, a clump of gas and dark matter in the process of collapsing and forming stars.
Analysis of light broken into its component wavelengths to determine a star's or planet's composition, temperature, and velocity.

gloss.footer: Essential terms for reading Webb discovery papers.

ipachart.title: English front vowels
ipachart.caption: The vowel quadrilateral maps tongue position: front → back across the top, close → open down the side. “beat”, “bit” and “bat” step steadily downward and forward.
ipachart.footer: Lengthening ɪ toward iː is the single biggest cue for “bit” → “beat”.

scriptstroke.title: Writing 木 (tree)

strokes.hint: Horizontal — left to right across the top.
Vertical — straight down through the centre.
Left-falling stroke — down and out to the lower left.
Right-falling stroke — down and out to the lower right.

scriptstroke.caption: Four strokes: the crossbar first, then the trunk, then the two roots splaying out — top-to-bottom, left-before-right, the universal stroke-order rules.
scriptstroke.footer: Master the four roots of 木 and the radicals 林 (woods) and 森 (forest) become repetition, not new shapes.
